title: Tourtière
subtitle: the Québec Christmas Eve meat pie: pork and beef gently spiced with cinnamon and clove, bound with potato under a golden crust
imageAlt: A golden double-crust meat pie with one wedge cut out on a white plate on a navy napkin
servingsNote: one 23 cm deep pie, 6 wedges: dinner for two, plus 4 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: The filling has to cool before it goes into the pastry (30 minutes, included), so it's easy to make the filling the day before.
Bake on a baking sheet on the lower rack so the bottom crust cooks through.
Warm, not hot: the cinnamon, clove and allspice are background notes, not heat.

items.name: russet potatoes
items.note: medium (about 250 g), peeled and cut in 1 cm dice

steps.title: Brown the meat
steps.text: Cook the pork and beef in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it up, 8–10 minutes until no pink remains. Spoon off all but about 1 tbsp of the fat.

steps.title: Onion and spices
steps.text: Add the onion and cook 4–5 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, salt, pepper, dried thyme, dried sage, cinnamon, cloves and allspice and cook 30 seconds.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the potato and broth, cover and simmer on low about 20 minutes, until the potato is very tender. Uncover, mash the potato into the meat with a potato masher and simmer 3–5 minutes more, until no liquid pools in the pan.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Spread the filling in a shallow dish and cool 30 minutes (or cover and refrigerate up to 2 days). Take the pie shells out of the freezer for the last 10 minutes. Put a baking sheet on the lower rack and heat the oven to 200°C (400°F).

steps.title: Fill and top
steps.text: Pack the filling into one shell and level it. Tip the second shell out of its foil pan onto the filling, press the edges together and crimp. Cut 4 slits in the top and brush with the beaten egg.

steps.title: Bake hot
steps.text: Set the pie on the hot baking sheet and bake 15 minutes.

steps.title: Finish low
steps.text: Lower the oven to 180°C (350°F) and bake 30–35 minutes more, until deep golden. If the edges brown too fast, cover them with strips of foil.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Rest 10 minutes, then cut into 6 wedges.

fixIt.fix: The filling was warm or the sheet wasn't preheated. Cool the filling fully and bake on the hot sheet on the lower rack.
It was still frozen. Let it soften 10 minutes, then pinch the cracks together; the egg wash hides them.
It simmered too long uncovered. Stop when no liquid pools; a few spoons of broth bring it back before filling.
Rest it the full 10 minutes, and mash the potato well; it's what holds the slices together.

saleTip: Ground pork is one of the cheapest meats at No Frills, often $3.99–4.99 a pound on sale. Pie shells go on sale before Christmas; keep a pack in the freezer.
swap: All pork: use 675 g ground pork and skip the beef. That's the most traditional Québec version.
leftovers: Cold or warm wedges for lunch, with a spoon of cranberry sauce or ketchup on the side.
doneness: The filling is fully cooked on the stove: ground pork and beef to 71°C (160°F) (Health Canada). The pie is done when the crust is deep golden. Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested Québec tourtière methods (Canadian Living, Ricardo): pork and beef simmered with potato and warm spices, cooled, then baked in a double crust at 200°C then 180°C.
prepAhead: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead and keep it covered in the fridge.
Assemble the whole pie and freeze it unbaked, wrapped well, up to 3 months. Bake from frozen at 190°C (375°F) on the hot sheet, 60–75 minutes, until golden and 74°C (165°F) in the centre.
reheat: Cover with foil and warm at 180°C (350°F) 25–30 minutes for a whole pie, 15 for a wedge, until 74°C (165°F) in the centre. The microwave works for one slice but softens the crust.

basic.note: Cinnamon only for the spice, and no garlic or dried sage.

stepNotes.1: Basic: just salt, pepper, dried thyme and cinnamon.

fancy.note: A touch of maple in the filling and a glossy cream wash, served with cranberry sauce.

stepNotes.2: Fancy: stir the maple syrup in after mashing.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: beat the cream into the egg instead of water for a deeper, shinier crust.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Serve wedges with a spoon of cranberry orange sauce on the side.

plating: Cut at the table so everyone sees the filling.
Cranberry sauce in a small bowl beside the pie.
Simple green salad or pickles on the side.

why.0-4: Mashed potato binds the filling so wedges hold their shape when cut.
why.0-12: Allspice, cinnamon and clove are what make it taste like tourtière, in amounts you notice but can't pick out.
why.1-1: The egg wash gives a deep golden, shiny crust.

funFact: Tourtière is traditionally eaten in Québec after midnight Mass on Christmas Eve, at the réveillon. The name likely comes from the deep dish it was baked in, a tourtière.

keeps.note: wrap whole or in wedges; unbaked pies freeze well too

pairs: the classic sweet-tart side for tourtière
